Winter Pack Down Guide

Winter welfare for your bees video

The time to perform a winter pack down is around April 25th

STEP:1|Have all equipment you require including extra boxes including storage boxes. It is important to have a plan of how and what you are preparing to do.
STEP:2|Set up your gear around the hive so once you start you are not trying to look for anything. It is a good idea to have three areas to put the frames you remove from the hive: one for brood frames, one for honey frames and the other for empty frames.|WINTER_PACKDOWN_02.PNG
STEP:3|Smoke the bees. Wait a minute for it to take effect.
STEP:4|Remove the lid. It is a good idea to turn the lid upside down and put a spare super on it. This is where you put your brood frames. The reason for this: if you accidentally have the queen on one of your frames and she drops off, she will land in the lid and not on the ground.|WINTER_PACKDOWN_04.PNG
STEP:5|Look into the top of the box and count the frames of bees. The frame should be fully covered on both sides with bees to be a 'full frame'. Otherwise, gauge from two or more frames with partial bee numbers to 'estimate' the number of full frames you have. This will depend on how far you can pack the bees down.|WINTER_PACKDOWN_05.PNG
STEP:6|Start removing the frames as you would if you were checking the hive, except separate the frames - brood in one box, honey frames in another box and the empty frames in another box. Keep trying to find the queen on each frame until located.|WINTER_PACKDOWN_06A.PNG,WINTER_PACKDOWN_06B.PNG,WINTER_PACKDOWN_06C.PNG,WINTER_PACKDOWN_06D.PNG
STEP:7|Remove the empty super and view the next super (or brood box if no other supers) - again look into the top of the box and count the frames of bees. This will depend on how far you can pack the bees down.|WINTER_PACKDOWN_07.PNG
STEP:8|Start removing the frames as you did in Step 6 - separating the frames - brood in one box, honey frames in another box and the empty frames in another box.|WINTER_PACKDOWN_08A.PNG,WINTER_PACKDOWN_08B.PNG
STEP:9|Continue steps 5 to 8 until you have inspected all the supers and brood box.|WINTER_PACKDOWN_09A.PNG,WINTER_PACKDOWN_09B.PNG,WINTER_PACKDOWN_09C.PNG
STEP:10|Now count up your frames to estimate the total number of frames of bees. This is a guide to the number of honey frames required. Try and have 1 brood frame to 1 capped honey frame.
STEP:11|Start replacing the frames. If you are packing down to one super - positions 1 & 8 are usually for honey frames, then from position 7 to 2. Try and have the honey frames on the outside and the brood frames in the middle. If you are packing down to 2 supers - the main preference is to have the majority of the brood frames in the bottom super. Say 5 in the bottom and 3 in the second super, always in the centre. Also ensure there is space for the queen to lay. Do not put frames with a lot of nectar as this may ferment over the cooler months and cause nosema or other issues. If you are packing down to 2 supers it is a good idea to remove the queen excluder to allow the queen to roam between both boxes.|WINTER_PACKDOWN_11.PNG,WINTER_PACKDOWN_11B.PNG,WINTER_PACKDOWN_11C.PNG
STEP:12|Once you have all frames in place, put your hive mat and lid in place. Secure your hive with an emlock or other method. At this point lift the back of the hive and feel the weight. You will perform this over winter to check to see if the bees have food. As food is consumed the weight will lessen and if too light, you may need to feed the bees. Please note, if you don't have enough honey frames as above, you will have to monitor the weight of the hive and feed them during winter.|WINTER_PACKDOWN_12.PNG
STEP:13|Remove all surplus frames and boxes. If you have honey frames, you can extract or store for the bees in early spring; remove all nectar from the frames. It is best to freeze all these frames for at least 3 days to kill off any wax moth larvae. Store in clear, sealed containers.|WINTER_PACKDOWN_13.PNG
